h2: Explore every Portable Cabin with Toilet size & its applications
intro: Nine standard sizes, one self-contained concept. A room with one attached washroom, priced ex-factory and delivered in 7–21 working days.

panels.paragraph: The compact self-contained unit: a small room with one corner washroom partitioned off, delivered plumbed and ready. Inside 100 sq ft you get a private usable room plus its own WC and washbasin behind a separate door, nothing external to build or share. It suits a single staffed point that must stand alone: a gate, a farm, a kiosk posting. Choose site-connected plumbing where lines exist, or the self-contained option where they don’t. The washroom door, vent and light are standard, and the same 5–10 year structural warranty applies.
panels.imageAlt: Portable cabin with toilet 10×10 ft, elevated view, relocatable room with one attached washroom by SAMAN Portable

panels.h3: 20×8 ft: the slim room-plus-washroom for narrow plots
panels.paragraph: A slim room-plus-washroom that travels on a standard trailer: usable space at one end, the attached washroom at the other, keeping the working area clear of the wet zone. The 160 sq ft narrow body fits plot margins, toll lines and corridor sites where a 10 ft deep unit cannot go. Duty staff get a private room and their own sanitation in one liftable piece, with supply and waste points that disconnect cleanly for the next move. It is the size most often repeated in multiples along a route, one self-contained room per posting.
panels.imageAlt: Portable cabin with toilet 20×8 ft, elevated view, relocatable room with one attached washroom by SAMAN Portable

panels.paragraph: Our most-ordered with-toilet size: a comfortable 200 sq ft main room with one partitioned washroom, moved as a single plumbed unit. The room takes a bed and desk, or a consultation setup, while the washroom keeps its own door and vent. It is the default when one room must work and stay on its own: rural postings, project stays, caretaker residences. MS and FRP shells carry the same layout; the material changes durability, not the plan. Compare it against the 20×12 if the stay runs beyond a season, the wider room earns its keep in comfort.
panels.imageAlt: Portable cabin with toilet 20×10 ft, elevated view, relocatable room with one attached washroom by SAMAN Portable

panels.h3: 20×12 ft: extra depth for the long stay
panels.paragraph: The added width goes entirely to the living and working area. The washroom stays compact at one end while the 240 sq ft main room gains space for a bed and a desk together, or a consultation area with a waiting corner. It is the comfortable long-stay size: supervisors posted for a full project phase pick it over the 20×10 for exactly that extra room. One unit, one washroom, one lift when the posting ends. The washroom keeps the standard WC and washbasin fittings. Power, lighting and AC provision are fitted through the room zone, with the washroom on its own circuit point.
panels.imageAlt: Portable cabin with toilet 20×12 ft, elevated view, relocatable room with one attached washroom by SAMAN Portable

panels.h3: 30×10 ft: the staffed rural deployment unit
panels.paragraph: A long 300 sq ft plan with a generous main room and the partitioned washroom at the far end. The common choice for a staffed rural or residential deployment that must relocate as one piece. The length lets the room zone into sleeping and working areas without touching the wet end. Outreach clinics and crew postings use it as a self-sufficient base: place it, connect or run self-contained, and it serves the full deployment. Because it moves as one piece, redeployment needs only transport and a prepared base, no rebuild at the new site.
panels.imageAlt: Portable cabin with toilet 30×10 ft, elevated view, relocatable room with one attached washroom by SAMAN Portable

panels.h3: 40×8 ft: the long, slim unit for linear sites
panels.paragraph: An extended usable space with sanitation attached, built to move on a 40 ft open trailer. The 320 sq ft slim body suits linear sites where units sit in a row along the work front. Each crew room keeping its own washroom instead of sharing a distant block. Pipeline, highway and corridor projects place several in line, and every unit remains individually liftable and reusable on the next stretch. Water and waste points sit at the washroom end, so row hookups stay short and serviceable. Each unit carries its own vent and light in the washroom, so a row stays serviceable without shared infrastructure.
applications: Crew rest rooms on linear projects
panels.imageAlt: Portable cabin with toilet 40×8 ft, elevated view, relocatable room with one attached washroom by SAMAN Portable

panels.h3: 20×20 ft: the square open plan with washroom
panels.paragraph: Four hundred square feet on a square footprint. A roomy open area with one attached washroom, engineered to stay liftable and reusable across sites. The square plan gives a hall-like space a corridor unit can’t: multi-bed crew quarters, a family-style stay unit, or a training and rest room with private sanitation. Confirm site access for the 20 ft wide load early; after that it plans like a small building that still moves. The washroom sits at one corner, leaving an uninterrupted main floor the full width of the unit.
panels.imageAlt: Portable cabin with toilet 20×20 ft, elevated view, relocatable room with one attached washroom by SAMAN Portable

panels.paragraph: A spacious main room with its attached washroom, sized to travel as one piece on a 40 ft trailer. The 400 sq ft length zones into sleeping, working and storage areas while the single washroom serves the whole unit from one end. It is the remote-camp workhorse. Long postings where one unit must be both residence and workspace, delivered plumbed and lifted out complete when the camp closes. Partition positions for the sleeping and work zones are set on the approved drawing. The 40 ft length still lifts as one unit, so the whole quarters relocate in a single trailer movement.
panels.imageAlt: Portable cabin with toilet 40×10 ft, elevated view, relocatable room with one attached washroom by SAMAN Portable

panels.h3: 40×12 ft: the largest single liftable unit
panels.paragraph: The most room-plus-washroom floor you can lift and reuse as one cabin: 480 sq ft that partitions into a multi-room layout on the approved drawing, with the single washroom serving the whole unit. Managers and in-charges posted long-term run it as a residence; large camps use it as the head unit. At ₹1,380 per square foot it carries the lowest rate on this ladder, beyond it, layouts become joined multi-module quotes. It is the practical ceiling of the one-unit concept. Everything above it is planned as a joined layout.
panels.imageAlt: Portable cabin with toilet 40×12 ft, elevated view, relocatable room with one attached washroom by SAMAN Portable
